newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on platinum rise.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on platinum rise.

text.p: Hong Kong gold powered higher on Friday to end above New York's close on speculative buying, short-covering and Japanese buying after platinum prices jumped, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$361.30/80 an ounce against New York's US$358.90/359.40 close on Thursday.
"The market is nervous," said a senior bullion dealer at a local firm.
"People are all focusing on platinum," another source said.
Higher platinum prices dragged gold up as Japanese buyers bought gold and sold platinum, some sources said. Others said speculative buying in afternoon trade made the market choppy.
Local gold ended HK$53 higher at HK$3,341 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +2.00 from its previous fix at nil.
"The buyer of gold has to pay HK$2 to the seller of gold," said an exchange source. "People were buying as much as possible, in anticipation of the prices going up more."
